The criterion is specifically about duplicate paragraph nodes in delivered markup and their containment/behavior. Normal-flow content and scrolling were directly observed, but the only text extraction sees one copy and cannot reveal an inert/hidden duplicate. Therefore neither satisfaction nor failure is defensible from the available evidence.

The correct letter route was verified, but the decisive claims—presence of a faint animated speckle and its placement above the film/still frame yet below the darkening panel—could not be directly observed with the available evidence. Reporting false would improperly treat missing layer-level evidence as proof of absence.
The shop has one visible five-item catalogue arrangement, with no UI for searching, filtering, or sorting. Its order is demonstrably not based on price or product name, so it meets the criterion.

Two distinct shop product pages render Specifications as repeated labelled row pairs with every figure/value in the same second column, not as prose. The consistent tabular extraction across Sensor and optics and Body sections provides direct structural evidence of a labelled table and aligned value column.

The criterion is composite and specifically requires the rejection path. Although an accepted quantity edit updated in place without a page reload, the observations do not verify the required pending-totals semantics or rollback-with-reason behavior on server rejection. Therefore the evidence cannot defensibly resolve satisfaction.
The discontinued Monitor Mount product page directly states both that the product is no longer sold and the exact date through which support continues, satisfying the criterion.

The fallback explanation correctly names supported browsers and offers the Arranger application path, but it is not shown in place of the connection control. A clickable connect control remains rendered in a browser the installer itself identifies as lacking direct camera capability, which is the evaluation rule's explicit no condition.

The cart directly labels both delivery/shipping and tax as estimates before an address is supplied and explicitly says the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known. The later payment summary switches to final labels, so the cart does not misrepresent the pre-address figures as final.

The criterion specifically requires observing how an expired warranty appears on the account camera grid. All directly observed warranty dates were future dates, so there is no defensible evidence that an expired warranty is rendered neutrally rather than as a warning or error.

All four surfaces named by R10 were directly visited in the authenticated customer session. Their visible content and measured controls consistently show dense, utilitarian layouts, with no observed marketing hero, decorative illustration, or oversized hero composition. The criterion is therefore satisfied.

The measured styles establish the intended polarity across the composite surfaces: the letter and its footer use light type, while the shop, cart, and authenticated account/commerce shell use dark type; the shop product ground was explicitly measured near-white. These observations satisfy R11.

Measured foreground, background, border, and outline colors across the supplied landing route and representative shop/product screens were exclusively neutral whites, grays, and near-black. Thus the allowed saturated accent occurs zero times on the observed screens, satisfying the 'at most once' requirement, and no text was found on an accent-colored background.

The relevant hover/focus/press-related motion across shop, account navigation, and cart consistently uses one short 120 ms linear timing. Direct CDP captures and computed styles agree, with no observed spring or visibly conflicting duration. Non-animated controls do not introduce contradictory motion.

Observed success, failure, and in-progress states across shop and account workflows all had explicit written labels in the rendered snapshot. No observed tested state relied on colour or movement alone.

Direct wide-versus-phone observations establish the required responsive transformation: the persistent left rail at desktop width collapses to one Menu control above the content column at phone width. The same narrow replacement was verified on both shop and cart, and the desktop rail includes the Account section links, supporting that this is the shared shop/cart/account rail.

The observed availability validation did not self-dismiss, but it was a quantity-limit error rather than a notice that an already-carted item's price or availability had changed. No actual cart price/availability-change notice could be induced and timed, so the criterion cannot be settled defensibly.

The criterion is satisfied because the letter itself carries explicit prices in a paragraph. Under the negative-polarity rule, this is a defect even though no form field or extra visible navigation beyond the wordmark/footer was observed.
